---
pagetitle: "Prompt, Check, Publish: a free e-book by Ravi Kalia"
# Quarto writes this into the share tags too; the setup cell checks it against book/_quarto.yml.
description: "Free e-book. A practitioner's guide to reproducible publishing: write once in Markdown, let a coding assistant write the code, check its work, and rebuild one source into a web page, Word, PDF, slides, an e-book, a website, a blog and a dashboard."
lang: en-GB
# The landing page for the book (book/). It is built with the book's own method: every
# number, the contents, the fan of formats and the quotations are read from the book's
# source and data by the cells below (_source.py), never typed. README.md, "The e-book
# landing page", explains how to rebuild it and its media.
format:
  html:
    # No Bootstrap or Quarto page furniture: the page loads only its own CSS and JS.
    minimal: true
    page-layout: custom
    css: ebook.css
    include-in-header: _head.html
    include-after-body:
      - text: '<script src="ebook.js"></script>'
execute:
  echo: false
resources:
  - ebook.js
  - media/*
  - media/fonts/*
---

```{python}
#| label: setup
import re

from IPython.display import Markdown

import _source as S
from _parts import raw
import _parts as P


def link(text: str, href: str) -> Markdown:
    """A Markdown link for an inline expression (a link target cannot hold one)."""
    return Markdown(f"[{text}]({href})")


m = S.meta()
formats = S.format_links()
n_formats = S.words(len(formats))
size = S.epub_size()
toc = S.contents()
london = S.london_top()
water = S.water_span()
cost, cost_checked = S.assistant_cost()
accounts, accounts_checked = S.assistant_accounts()
chart = S.cell_figure("book/chapters/05-compute.qmd", "fig-ldn-top10")
appx = {a["label"]: a for a in toc["appendices"]}
parts = toc["parts"]
ch2, ch3 = parts[0]["chapters"][1]["href"], parts[0]["chapters"][2]["href"]

# The page's <head> and its <title> must agree with the book (scripts/ebook_media.py writes it).
S.check_head()
header = S.read("ebook/index.qmd")
if (re.search(r'^pagetitle: "(.+)"$', header, re.M).group(1),
        re.search(r'^description: "(.+)"$', header, re.M).group(1)) != S.share_text():
    raise ValueError("pagetitle or description no longer matches book/_quarto.yml (_source.share_text)")
# The deck's Get the Book slide links here with a QR code (scripts/deck_qr.py).
deck_url = re.search(r'^ebook-qr:\n(?:  .*\n)*?  url: "([^"]+)"', S.read("index.qmd"), re.M).group(1)
if deck_url != S.PAGE_URL:
    raise ValueError(f"index.qmd's ebook-qr url {deck_url} is not {S.PAGE_URL}")

# Wording the page quotes, which must still be the book's.
PREFACE = "book/index.qmd"
LOOP = [
    ("Prompt", "Describe one small piece of work to a coding assistant, with its files and columns named."),
    ("Check", "Read what changed, look at the result, compare it with the data. An assistant can be "
              "fluent, fast and wrong, so this step is never skipped, and it is always yours."),
    ("Publish", "Quarto rebuilds every output from the checked source, the same way every time."),
]
S.quote(PREFACE, "one small piece of work with its files and columns named",
        "read what changed, look at the result, compare it with the data",
        "An assistant can be fluent, fast and wrong, so this step is never skipped, and it is always yours",
        "every output from the checked source the same way every time",
        "No programming is assumed",
        "a computer on which you can install software (Windows, Mac or Linux), a free GitHub account, "
        "and an account with one coding assistant",
        "the exact prompt to give your assistant, what it will probably run, and the few things only you can do",
        "a web page, a Word brief for partners, a printed flyer, a dashboard for managers and a published website",
        "publish the analysis as a report, slides, a blog post and a website, all from one analysis script")
S.quote("book/about-author.qmd", "PhD", "University of Oxford", "written edition")
S.quote("book/appendices/i-workshop.qmd", "six-hour, hands-on workshop")
S.quote("book/copyright.qmd", "were checked on the dates given in the text and will change")
# The contents' introduction names the first and last appendices.
if not (appx["A"]["title"].startswith("Windows") and appx["J"]["title"] == "Glossary"):
    raise ValueError("the appendices changed: reword the contents' introduction")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(P.hero(f"Write once. Let an assistant write the code. Check it. Publish to {n_formats} formats.", size))
```

## One loop, every step {#the-loop}

You ask, you check, Quarto rebuilds. Every hands-on step in the book goes once round this
loop, so a mistake is caught while it is still small.

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(P.loop(LOOP))
```
:::
:::

## One `.qmd` file, `{python} n_formats` outputs {#one-source}

The fan on the cover is the book's promise: one plain-text source, rebuilt into every format
with one command. Each line below leads to a real one.

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(P.fan(formats))
```

    f"{water['first']}–{water['last']}",

    "and publish the analysis as a report, slides, a blog post and a website, all from one "
    "analysis script.",
    P.clip("colombia-relief", "colombia-relief-orbit"),

) + "</div>")

### This page was built the way the book teaches {#how-this-page-was-made}

This page is a Quarto document. When it is built, code reads the book's data, chapter list
and cover, so every number on it, the contents below and the fan of formats above come from
the book's source, not from typing. Change the data, rebuild, and the page changes with it.
This is the function behind the London number:

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw(P.code(S.london_top))
```

1. A computer on which you can install software: Windows, Mac or Linux.
2. A free [GitHub](https://github.com/signup) account.
3. An account with one coding assistant.

## Run it as a six-hour workshop {#the-workshop}

The book is the written edition of a six-hour, hands-on workshop. Its slides are online, and
its worked examples and catch-up checkpoints are in the repository, so you can follow along
alone or teach it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
raw('<p class="links">' + "".join(
    f'<a href="{P.e(h)}">{P.e(t)}{P.ICON["right"]}</a>' for t, h in [
        ("Workshop slides", S.DECK_URL), ("GitHub repository", S.REPO),
        ("Catch-up checkpoints", f"{S.REPO}/tree/main/checkpoints"),
        (f"Appendix I: {appx['I']['title']}", appx["I"]["href"])]) + "</p>")
```

## Before you download {#faq-heading}

<details>
<summary>Is it really free?</summary>

Yes. Download the EPUB or read the website edition: there is no sign-up and no email to give.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Which assistant do I need?</summary>

One coding assistant. `{python} accounts` (checked `{python} accounts_checked`).
`{python} link("Chapter 2", ch2 + "#sec-choose")` explains how to choose, and
`{python} link("what a conversation costs", ch2 + "#sec-cost")`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Does it work on Windows?</summary>

Yes: Windows, Mac or Linux. On Windows you first install Ubuntu with WSL;
`{python} link("Appendix A", appx["A"]["href"])` and the workshop's
[Windows page](../windows-setup.html) take you through it, one checked step at a time.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How current is it?</summary>

The first edition, of `{python} S.month_year(m["date"])`, was checked with Quarto
`{python} S.checked_with()`. Prices, versions, screens and plans are given with the date they
were checked, and will change.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Can I teach with it?</summary>

Yes: teach from the free book and slides, link to them, and follow
`{python} link("Appendix I", appx["I"]["href"])` to run the workshop. To copy or adapt the material,
[ask the author first](https://github.com/project-delphi/quarto-workshop/issues).

</details>

<details>
<summary>How was it written?</summary>

With an AI coding assistant, as the book teaches. From the book's AI usage statement:

> `{python} S.ai_statement()`

</details>
:::
:::
